paragraphs: Rav Yitzchak the son of Rav.

Yuchasin and Seder HaDorot mention him without giving a citation. Hyman finds that reading in the Rif and Rosh on [Moed Katan 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.17b.2): “What is tavra? Rav Yitzchak son of Rav said…” Hyman prefers a Rif manuscript that reads Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehudah, as cited in Dikdukei Soferim.[^1]

As for [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.3.1.13), with the additional historical folio locator 2b, where Hyman gives Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rav, Hyman explained under Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Chiyya Kahuna that the reading should be son of Rabbi Chiyya Kahuna there.[^2][^3]

notes.text: Hyman proposes Rav Yehudah for the first father-name and Chiyya Kahuna for the second. The two claims are preserved without identifying every abbreviated Rav as the same person.
The supplied Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot locator is chapter 3, halakhah 1, with the additional folio locator ב:, rendered 2b. It is not a range of halakhot 1–2.

The linked Bavli reads “Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehudah.” Hyman cites the shorter form from the Rif and Rosh and the longer one from a Rif manuscript. The linked Yerushalmi reads “Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi [Chiyya] Ketubah,” translated there as “Chiyya the Scribe.” Hyman proposes Chiyya Kahuna.
